page.layout: One page of text: verse stanzas in one column at the top, then a right-aligned reference "I. I. B.", a woodcut ornament in the centre, and a right-aligned heading "IN GAL." below it. Running head at top; page number at top left.

p.i: Indigenas Gallos nunquam hospes auarus amabit, Sibi suisque proximus.
Proditione, dolis, scelere, atque libidine & ira Opes parabit impias.
Hac animis potior sistat sententia vestris, Vos vos labantes eriget.
Sed cùm aduersa trahant Gallorum fata nepotes, Vanæ querelæ nil iuuant.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament between the reference and the heading: a stylised mask (a face with snakes or tendrils, flanked by foliage and hanging tassels). It is an illustration, not text, so not transcribed. The verse lines are set in italic with a long s; the long s has been written as a plain s. Running head reads "Gvisiaca." in small capitals, rendered with the u/v rule as GUISIACA. The verse stanzas are shown with the printed line breaks inside each paragraph. No catchword or signature is visible at the foot of the page.
